chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: What the jam sessions played and Leo Watson as scat king
summary: He describes the blues and standards jammed on and the scat singing of Leo Watson at Billy Berg's.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, naturally, they were playing the Blues for one thing, and I can't think of...whatever tunes they used to jam on. They used to play "China Boy" and those kind of things, you know, or "Liza" with the changes, and "Honeysuckle Rose" and all those kind of things that guys used to jam on in those days.
So I will never forget hearing Charlie Christian and Jimmy Blanton, and Teddy Bunn and Leo Watson with his... He was the boss scat vocalist. Scatman retained the name for
years, and still does, but Leo Watson was the king. Then there was Slim and Slam... Well, it was just an orgy of good music.
Was there a regular broadcast from that Billy Berg's?
